terms.comment: Said in Petronius by a freedman at Trimalchio’s dinner, after “not today, then tomorrow”.
We have found no classical instance of vīta fert on its own; Cicero uses ferre so with ut: ut aetās illa fert, as is usual at that age (Clu. 168, Lewis & Short s.v. ferō).

phrases.latin: quod hodiē nōn est, crās erit: sīc vīta trūditur
phrases.english: what isn’t today will be tomorrow: that’s how life goes on

sources: Lewis & Short: trudo · Lewis & Short: fero
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 339.
Petronius quoted from the Latinitas loci collection loci-petronius, checked against the edition named there.
